question:
A 74-year-old woman with a history of gastric bypass surgery presents with a two-month history of
fatigue and leg swelling. Her vital signs include a heart rate of 85/min, blood pressure of 127/66 mmHg,
respiratory rate of 20/min, and she is afebrile. Physical examination reveals temporal wasting, loss of
subcutaneous fat, and atrophy of the upper arms and legs, along with 2+ pedal edema. Neurological
examination is normal. Laboratory findings show hemoglobin of 9 mg/dL with an MCV of 105, serum
albumin of 2.2 g/dL, and serum pre-albumin of 0.03 g/L (normal range: 0.2–0.4). Considering treatment
for her malnutrition, which of the following is the most likely cause of her clinical findings? Answer
Choices: (A) Protein malnutrition with thiamine deficiency (B) Mixed malnutrition with deficiencies in
fat-soluble vitamins (C) Severe calorie malnutrition with thiamine deficiency (D) Protein malnutrition
with niacin deficiency (E) Protein malnutrition with vitamin B12 deficiency (F) Vitamin D deficiency with
secondary protein malnutrition (G) Iron deficiency anemia with chronic protein malnutrition (H) Protein
malnutrition with secondary zinc deficiency (I) Protein malnutrition with folate deficiency (J) Chronic

malabsorption with vitamin B6 deficiency
 A. Iron deficiency anemia with chronic protein malnutrition
B. Severe calorie malnutrition with thiamine deficiency
C. Vitamin D deficiency with secondary protein malnutrition
D. Protein malnutrition with vitamin B12 deficiency
E. Chronic malabsorption with vitamin B6 deficiency
F. Protein malnutrition with niacin deficiency
G. Protein malnutrition with thiamine deficiency
H. Protein malnutrition with folate deficiency
I. Mixed malnutrition with deficiencies in fat-soluble vitamins
J. Protein malnutrition with secondary zinc deficiency
